notes.1.head: The sentence continues past the unit: its verb ('to break', rumpere) falls in the next line.
notes.7.351: Typographical slips in the text (Cauaseum, languesct, mediiis) are read as Caucaseum, languescit, mediis. 'monte' at 7.370 is marked by the edition as corrupt; translated literally. 'By Phoebe's tenth lamp' (lampade Phoebes sub decima) presumably means the tenth night of the moon.

nodes.text: The Argonautica of Gaius Valerius Flaccus, Book One.
We sing of the straits first crossed by the great sons of the gods,
and of the prophetic ship, which dared to seek
the shores of Scythian Phasis, and between the clashing ridges a course through the midst
and now the high groves of Rhodope groan: such a Lycurgus his frantic
wife and his children flee through the long colonnades.
Then Alcimede was bringing offerings to Tartarean Jove and to the Stygian
shades, anxious over so great a son,
[to see] if she could learn beforehand something better from the ghosts she had roused.
she turns, glad, for his sake alone, either to live
or to die, whichever he may wish. She prays for greater
spells, [prays] that Hecate send greater powers
into her now, and she did not rest content with familiar poisons.
Then her robe is girded up, and the flower, than which no power is more
trusted by her, from the blood of Prometheus' liver,
the Caucasian flower, she brings out, and grasses nourished by his torments,
which that sacred gore, among the snows and grim frosts,
hardens and feeds, when the vulture, the flesh devoured,
rises from the crags and sprinkles [it] from its open beak.
That same [blood] does not fade at the limits of a long age,
green and undying; that same blood stands firm against thunderbolts,
and in the midst of fires the herbs blossom.
Hecate first brought to it a sickle tempered in the springs of Styx
and dug the sturdy ears out of the crags;
afterwards the crop was shown to her handmaid, who, by Phoebe's
tenth lamp, reaps the teeming ridges and rages through all
the remains and gore of the god; he groans, powerless,
watching the Colchian's face; then all his limbs are drawn in
†on the mountain† by pain, and all the chains tremble beneath the sickle.
With such poisons, against her own kingdom, the unhappy girl
arms herself, and trembling goes out into the dark night.
